text:
A: Hiya, you alright? I'm Liam.
B: Hi! Riya. Yeah, good thanks, you?
A: Yeah, not bad, not bad. Just recovering from that puzzle, to be fair. The last one with the shapes nearly finished me off.
B: Oh my god, same, I literally just guessed the last few. I was like, it's fine, no one's gonna see this.
A: No one's gonna see it. There's probably a league table somewhere, knowing my luck. Where are you based then?
B: Leyton, East London. You?
A: Wakefield, West Yorkshire. So a bit of a way. What do you do, are you working, studying, or...?
B: Bit of both, kind of. Final year at Queen Mary, business management, and I work part-time on reception at a dental practice in Stratford.
A: No way. A dental practice? My girlfriend Jess is a dental nurse.
B: Shut up, really? Okay, so she'll know. The dentists always run late, right? Mine's like twenty minutes behind by ten in the morning, every day. And I'm the one at the front getting the looks.
A: Yeah, no, she says exactly that. She reckons reception get it worst, to be fair, cos you're the first face they see.
B: Honestly, yeah. Half the job's just calming people down, like, it's fine, it's a check-up, you'll survive. I actually like that bit. The admin, less so. Recall letters, don't ask.
A: I won't ask. What are you after when you finish then?
B: Erm, good question. Something in marketing, maybe brand partnerships, like beauty or fashion. I'm gonna sort the grad scheme stuff after my dissertation. That's the plan anyway.
A: After the dissertation, yeah. Fair. When's that due?
B: Don't. April. It's fine. What about you, what do you do?
A: So I'm in technical sales, commercial heating and air con. I look after about sixty trade accounts across West Yorkshire, so I'm out on site visits two, three days a week, quoting jobs, that kind of thing. It's a bit of a grind, but I'm top of the board at the minute, so I can't complain. And the car's a perk, I've got the Audi, which Jess thinks is a bit much.
B: Ooh, okay, top of the board. Is that like an actual board?
A: It's a screen in the office. Which is worse, do you know what I mean? Everyone can see it.
B: That's so much pressure, I'd hate that. I'd be bottom, guaranteed.
A: Nah, you'd smash it. You're good with people, you can tell. That's ninety percent of sales.
B: Aw, thank you. I'll put that on my CV. "Liam from Wakefield says."
A: References available on request. So what do you do for fun? London, there must be loads on.
B: Erm, honestly, brunch. Way too much brunch. Walthamstow, Hackney. And trashy TV. Are you watching The Traitors?
A: Jess has got me on it. I keep saying I'm not into it, and then I'm sat there going, it's him, it's obviously him.
B: No, totally, that's how it gets you. Do you go away much? I'm desperate for a proper holiday.
A: Yeah, we try and do two a year. Dubai last year, which was unreal, nice hotel, pool on the roof. Marbella the year before.
B: Oh my god, Dubai's literally my dream. Like properly, nice hotel, the whole thing. My boyfriend keeps saying we can't afford it.
A: That's what Jess says. She wants us saving for a house. She's probably right, to be fair. Don't tell her I said that.
B: Your secret's safe. Was that a golf bag behind you, by the way, in your picture?
A: It was, yeah. I took it up last year, mostly cos clients play. I'm terrible.
B: That's so corporate, I love it.
A: Guilty. Oh, is that the timer going?
B: I think so, yeah. Nice to meet you!
A: You too, Riya. Good luck with the dissertation!
